memory_lessons.applicability: Use the 4096-input result as a comparison point, not proof that further tile increases will help.
memory_lessons.claim: The recorded two-launch direct-output schedules were correct for 1024-, 2048-, and 4096-input tiles. Their measured means were about 16.93, 12.02, and 10.13 μs respectively; these are observed total-run timings, not evidence of a monotonic trend.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare the 8192-input candidate's full-domain correctness and total-run timing against the 4096-input result; if it regresses, retain the measured 4096-input option.

proposal.hypothesis: Using the existing CTA reduction with 8192 input values per first-stage CTA should produce 512 partials at n=4194304—half the 1024 from the previously measured 4096-input tile—while retaining 512 first-stage CTAs and the same two-launch direct-output schedule. This tests whether the reduced first-stage CTA count still supplies enough parallelism; it makes no performance claim and leaves the small-n path unchanged.

retained: For n > 32768, increase the first-stage tile from 2048 to 8192 inputs per CTA, using the same 128-thread shared-memory reduction.
Set the first-stage launch count to ceil(n/8192); for n=4194304 this reduces initialized partials from 2048 in the selected parent to 512.
Keep the final CTA reduction and direct write to out, and leave the small-n schedule unchanged.
